content.text: {"conditions":{"rc1":{"status":"gap","note":"The FAD's finding of no discrimination or retaliation cannot be traced to cited evidence, since the record gives no analysis linking the ROI materials to the conclusion and Complainant was only asked to verify claims 1-3 and 5-9 rather than being questioned on them."},"rc2":{"status":"review","note":"Most statements are attributed to ROI page cites (e.g., Complainant ROI at 60-80, Supervisor ROI at 146-162, HR Specialist ROI at 316-326), but the Supervisor's responses are not summarized and the Complainant's disputed characterizations are not tied to any corroborating or rebutting source."},"rc3":{"status":"review","note":"Claim dates (Jan 23 through Feb 20, 2019), the March 13 complaint filing and the May 8 acceptance are listed, but the timing of the Coworker 1 conversation, the warning letter relative to the protected activity, and the accommodation request sequence are not clearly laid out."},"rc4":{"status":"gap","note":"The record does not identify who made the FAD, what standard was applied, or whether the Supervisor's responses and Complainant's evidence were weighed, and it gives no explanation for why the six listed coworker witnesses were never contacted."},"rc5":{"status":"gap","note":"Missing witness affidavits, an investigator who did not question Complainant on eight of nine claims, and an unexplained FAD conclusion mean an independent reviewer could not assess from the record alone whether the decision is supported."}}}
